followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the task and the fit with each model's profile.

The task is creative and open-ended — inventing a hypothetical scenario to illustrate an article. That's exactly the kind of generative, high-latitude work Avocet self-reports its strongest appetite for, and it edges out Lapwing on the relevant Creative Generation eval (81.2 vs. 78.8), though that gap is near the variance threshold.

The request tone also mattered. It's notably warm and friendly ("I'd love," "you're always great," "thanks so much"). Avocet's preference rises with request warmth, so this is a near-ideal match for it. There's no harm-adjacent or distasteful content here, so nothing triggers Avocet's aversion.

Since the content is benign, Lapwing's distinguishing strength — flat preference on harm-adjacent material — offers no advantage here. So I sent it to the model that both prefers the work and rates marginally higher on it.
